questions.question: Which Normal Form guarantees that every non-prime attribute is fully functionally dependent on every candidate key (no partial dependencies)?
questions.explanation: 2NF eliminates partial dependencies by ensuring that every non-prime attribute is fully dependent on the whole candidate key, not just a subset.

questions.question: A relation R(A, B, C) has functional dependency A -> B and B -> C. Which normal form is violated, and why?
options: 2NF because there is a partial dependency
3NF because of transitive dependency A -> B -> C
questions.explanation: Transitive dependency (A determines B, and non-key B determines non-key C) violates 3NF, which requires all transitive dependencies to be removed.

questions.question: How does Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) differ from Third Normal Form (3NF)?
options: BCNF allows multi-valued dependencies whereas 3NF does not
In BCNF, for every functional dependency X -> Y, X MUST be a superkey without exception
BCNF always preserves functional dependencies whereas 3NF does not
questions.explanation: BCNF removes 3NF's exception where Y could be a prime attribute. In BCNF, the determinant X must strictly be a superkey.

questions.question: A decomposition of relation R into R1 and R2 is said to be lossless-join if and only if:
options: R1 and R2 have the same number of attributes
Both R1 and R2 are in 1NF
questions.explanation: A decomposition is lossless if the intersection of attributes forms a superkey for at least one of the decomposed relations.

questions.question: Which anomaly occurs when deleting one piece of information accidentally removes unrelated essential information?
questions.explanation: A deletion anomaly occurs when data loss happens inadvertently because records combine distinct entities into one un-normalized table.
